data.label: Synthetic user (browser)
data.description: A synthetic test user in a browser. This is a client reference and is not provisioned.

data.label: Chat web app
data.description: Hosts the chat UI from private S3 assets. Signs in with authorization code plus PKCE and calls the chat API with an access token.

data.label: User sign-in
data.description: A user pool with admin-created synthetic users and MFA. Issues JWTs whose subject defines who owns each conversation.

data.label: Chat API
data.description: An HTTP API with a JWT authorizer, request size limits and throttling. It rejects anonymous calls.

data.label: Chat orchestrator
data.description: Uses the JWT subject as the owner key and never trusts a user ID sent in the request. Builds a bounded context window from recent turns, enforces input and output limits, and calls the model with retries and timeouts. If the model fails, it returns a recoverable 'try again' response without losing the stored turn. It also handles conversation delete and escalation, and owns its execution role and logs.

data.label: Conversation store
data.description: Partition key: owner subject. Sort key: conversation and turn. Encrypted at rest. Delete removes every turn in the conversation. Optional TTL is still to be decided.

data.label: Foundation model
data.description: A direct foundation model through Converse. The model ID, access, region support and quotas are not yet verified. Local tests replace it with scripted responses.

data.label: Escalation queue
data.description: Receives an escalation record holding a snapshot of the user-approved conversation context. Encrypted, with a dead-letter queue for failed handling.

data.label: Human support reviewer
data.description: A person who picks up escalations. The tooling and access model are still to be decided.

data.label: Logs and alarms
data.description: Lambda and API metrics, a model-error alarm and an escalation DLQ alarm. Logs exclude message content.

brief.application: Use AWS for this synthetic architecture qualification. Build an authenticated conversational assistant for synthetic users. Include an application, per-user conversation state, model runtime, bounded context and an escalation path. No external actions in this first test. Acceptance criteria: One user cannot read another conversation; Context and response sizes are bounded; Model outage produces a recoverable response; Deleting a conversation removes its stored context; Escalation retains the approved conversation context. Draw the complete end-to-end architecture with concrete service choices and connected flows. Explain the first local test, distinguish mocked model behavior from actual model validation, and ask one useful missing-decision question. Do not reduce this application to storage to satisfy generator coverage. Do not invent successful deployment or approved region/account access.

decisions.subject: design.first-end-to-end-aws-conversational-assistant-sketch
decisions.title: First end-to-end AWS conversational assistant sketch
decisions.context: Scope: an authenticated chat assistant for synthetic users with per-user conversation state, bounded context, a Bedrock model, recovery when the model fails and a human escalation path. External actions are out of scope. Assumptions: the region and country are not yet chosen. The Bedrock model ID, model access and quotas have not been verified. Native generators do not yet cover this chat Lambda, the conversation table or the escalation queue, so those parts still need engineering work. This is a design intent only. Nothing has been deployed or validated.
decisions.decision: Drawn while talking as design revision 2.

needs.statement: A user can only read, continue or delete conversations owned by their authenticated subject. Requests for another user's conversation are denied.
needs.rationale: Without this, one user could read another user's chats.
needs.basis: User acceptance criterion: "One user cannot read another conversation".

needs.statement: Input, context window and model output have enforced maximum sizes. Oversized requests are rejected with a clear error.
needs.rationale: Size limits control cost and latency, and stop unbounded prompts. The exact limits shown are proposed defaults, not confirmed values.
needs.basis: User acceptance criterion: "Context and response sizes are bounded".

needs.statement: When the model fails or times out, the user gets a recoverable response and the stored conversation stays intact for a retry.
needs.rationale: A model outage must not lose or corrupt conversation state.
needs.basis: User acceptance criterion: "Model outage produces a recoverable response".

needs.statement: Deleting a conversation removes all of its stored turns and context from the conversation store.
needs.rationale: Users need real deletion, not just hiding. How escalation copies are retained is still an open question.
needs.basis: User acceptance criterion: "Deleting a conversation removes its stored context".

needs.statement: Escalation sends a snapshot of the user-approved conversation context to the human review queue, and that snapshot is retained there.
needs.rationale: Reviewers need the context the user approved, and only that context.
needs.basis: User acceptance criterion: "Escalation retains the approved conversation context".
